    "content": "<p>This post will contain whatever handy information I come across for utilizing\nthe SharePoint REST APIs with Microsoft Flow.</p>\n<!--more-->\n<p>Why would you want to do this? Because there aren't enough actions to accomplish\nall the things you'd want to do with SharePoint via Flow.</p>\n<p>The first section of this guide comes from combining a few different blog posts,\nbut I found\n<a href=\"https://blogs.u2u.be/u2u/post/calling-the-sharepoint-online-api-from-within-microsoft-flow\">Calling the SharePoint Online API from within Microsoft Flow by ROBRECHT-VAN-CAENEGEM</a>\nto be the most useful. It's got pictures!</p>\n<h1>How does this work?</h1>\n<ul>\n<li>Microsoft Flow can send generic HTTP requests, with custom headers, body, etc.</li>\n<li>For Flow to authenticate to SharePoint during the REST calls, we'll make use\nof the access tokens typically used for SharePoint Addins/Apps</li>\n</ul>\n<h1>Intial Setup</h1>\n<p>We're going to need four pieces of data:</p>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>CLIENTID</strong>: Unique id assigned to your add-in registration</li>\n<li><strong>CLIENTSECRET</strong>: Secret value used by your add-in registration</li>\n<li><strong>REALM</strong>: This is the unique id assigned to your SharePoint Online tenant.</li>\n<li><strong>TENANT</strong>: The hostname of your tenant (e.g. example.sharepoint.com)</li>\n</ul>\n<h2>Obtain the CLIENTID and CLIENTSECRET values</h2>\n<ol>\n<li>\n<p>On the SharePoint site that you need to communicate with, navigate to\nAppRegNew page</p>\n<pre><code>&lt;your site's URL&gt;/_layouts/15/appregnew.aspx\n</code></pre>\n</li>\n<li>\n<p>Fill in the information.</p>\n<ul>\n<li>Client Id: &lt;&lt;Generate It!&gt;&gt;</li>\n<li>Client Secret: &lt;&lt;Generate It!&gt;&gt;</li>\n<li>Title: &lt;<Project Name Flow>&gt;</li>\n<li>App Domain: localhost</li>\n<li>Redirect URI: https:/localhost</li>\n</ul>\n</li>\n<li>\n<p>Store the Client Id and Secret. We're going to need it for the next step.</p>\n</li>\n<li>\n<p>Click the <em>Create</em> button.</p>\n</li>\n<li>\n<p>Navigate to the AppInv page <code>&lt;your site's URL&gt;/_layouts/15/appinv.aspx</code></p>\n</li>\n<li>\n<p>Put the <em>Client Id</em> into the <em>App Id</em> text box and look it up.</p>\n</li>\n<li>\n<p>Paste the following XML into the <em>Permission Request XML</em> box\n(<a href=\"https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/sharepoint/dev/sp-add-ins/add-in-permissions-in-sharepoint\">modify as needed for what scope and right you need</a>):</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-xml\">&lt;AppPermissionRequests AllowAppOnlyPolicy=&quot;true&quot;&gt;\n    &lt;AppPermissionRequest Scope=&quot;http://sharepoint/content/sitecollection&quot; Right=&quot;FullControl&quot; /&gt;\n&lt;/AppPermissionRequests&gt;\n</code></pre>\n</li>\n<li>\n<p>Click the <em>Create</em> button.</p>\n</li>\n</ol>\n<h2>Obtain the REALM value</h2>\n<ol>\n<li>On the SharePoint site that you just finished app registration on, navigate\nto the AppPrincipals page<pre><code>/_layouts/15/AppPrincipals.aspx\n</code></pre>\n</li>\n<li>You should see your recently registered app principle along with an App\nIdentifier. The last section of the App Identifier, after the @, is the\nREALM value.</li>\n</ol>\n<h2>Setup Authentication in Flow</h2>\n<ol>\n<li>\n<p>In your created flow, directly after the trigger, do the following:</p>\n</li>\n<li>\n<p>Create a new <strong>Parse JSON</strong> action, renamed to <em>Authentication Values</em>,\nfilling in your own values and using the below schema.</p>\n<ul>\n<li>Content:<pre><code class=\"language-json\">{\n    &quot;realm&quot;: &quot;{REALM}&quot;,\n    &quot;clientId&quot;: &quot;{CLIENTID}&quot;,\n    &quot;clientSecret&quot;: &quot;{CLIENTSECRET}&quot;,\n    &quot;principal&quot;: &quot;00000003-0000-0ff1-ce00-000000000000&quot;,\n    &quot;tenant&quot;: &quot;{TENANT}&quot;\n}\n</code></pre>\n</li>\n<li>Schema:<pre><code class=\"language-json\">{\n    &quot;type&quot;: &quot;object&quot;,\n    &quot;properties&quot;: {\n        &quot;realm&quot;: { &quot;type&quot;: &quot;string&quot; },\n        &quot;clientId&quot;: { &quot;type&quot;: &quot;string&quot; },\n        &quot;clientSecret&quot;: { &quot;type&quot;: &quot;string&quot; },\n        &quot;principal&quot;: { &quot;type&quot;: &quot;string&quot; },\n        &quot;tenant&quot;: { &quot;type&quot;: &quot;string&quot; }\n    }\n}\n</code></pre>\n</li>\n</ul>\n</li>\n<li>\n<p>Create a new <strong>Initialize variable</strong> action, renamed to Initialize\nAccessTokenBody, with the following values: - Name: <code>AccessTokenBody</code> -\nType: String - Value:\n<code>concat('grant_type=client_credentials&amp;client_id=', body('Authentication_Values')?['clientId'], '@', body('Authentication_Values')?['realm'], '&amp;client_secret=', body('Authentication_Values')?['clientSecret'], '&amp;resource=', body('Authentication_Values')?['principal'], '/', body('Authentication_Values')?['tenant'], '@', body('Authentication_Values')?['realm']) </code></p>\n</li>\n<li>\n<p>Create a new <strong>HTTP - HTTP</strong> action.</p>\n</li>\n<li>\n<p>Rename it <em>Get Access Token</em></p>\n</li>\n<li>\n<p>Fill in the values:</p>\n<ul>\n<li><strong>Method</strong>: POST</li>\n<li><strong>Uri</strong>:\n<code>https://accounts.accesscontrol.windows.net/@{body('Authentication_Values')?['realm']}/tokens/oauth/2</code></li>\n<li><strong>Headers</strong>:<pre><code class=\"language-json\">{\n    &quot;Content-Type&quot;: &quot;application/x-www-form-urlencoded&quot;\n}\n</code></pre>\n</li>\n<li><strong>Body</strong>: the <em>AccessTokenBody</em> variable</li>\n</ul>\n</li>\n<li>\n<p>Add a new <strong>Parse JSON</strong> action and rename it <strong>Parse Access Token</strong>.</p>\n</li>\n<li>\n<p>Content should be set to the Body parameter from the previuos step. Schema\nshould be set to the following:</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-json\">{\n    &quot;type&quot;: &quot;object&quot;,\n    &quot;properties&quot;: {\n        &quot;token_type&quot;: { &quot;type&quot;: &quot;string&quot; },\n        &quot;access_token&quot;: { &quot;type&quot;: &quot;string&quot; }\n    }\n}\n</code></pre>\n</li>\n</ol>\n<p>With this setup, you should be able to test your FLOW and not have it error. You\ncan also check and see the token_type and access_token being parsed. Note that\nthe most tricky part of this is getting the Body variable of step 6 setup\ncorrectly. Note that my value depends upon you having renamed the steps as I\ninstructed to work.</p>\n<p><strong>You're now ready to start using SharePoint REST APIs in Flow!</strong></p>\n<h1>Helpful Snippets</h1>\n<p>This section will be a hodge podge of useful snippets I plan to continue adding\nto.</p>\n<h2>General</h2>\n<h3>Headers</h3>\n<p>It's easiest to paste in the headers values of <strong>HTTP - HTTP</strong> actions if it's\nin text mode. Here's what's needed (adjust the name of the action where mine\nsays <strong>Parse Access Token</strong> to match the name of your action that parses the\naccess tokens)</p>\n<pre><code class=\"language-json\">{\n    &quot;Authorization&quot;: &quot;@{body('Parse Access Token')?['token_type']} @{body('Parse Access Token')?['access_token']}&quot;,\n    &quot;Accept&quot;: &quot;application/json;odata=verbose&quot;,\n    &quot;Content-Type&quot;: &quot;application/json;odata=verbose&quot;\n}\n</code></pre>\n<h2>Groups and Permissions</h2>\n<h3>Set the Owner of a SharePoint Group to another SharePoint Group</h3>\n<p>So, this apparently has been broken via typical REST API method calls for quite\nsome time. There is a working alternative though - manually construct the call\nthat the CSOM library would have made. The best resource I found for this is\n<a href=\"http://www.jrjlee.com/2014/01/custom-workflow-activity-for-setting.html\">Jason Lee's blog post: Custom Workflow Activity for Setting a SharePoint Group Owner</a>,\nwhich is specifically talking about doing this within a SharePoint 2013 model\nworkflow. We'll modify it slightly.</p>\n<ol>\n<li>Start with your standard <strong>HTTP - HTTP</strong> action.</li>\n<li>Method = POST</li>\n<li>Uri (adjust values for your environment) =\n<code>https://{TENANT}/{SPSITE_URL}/_vti_bin/client.svc/ProcessQuery</code></li>\n<li>Headers are slightly different than the Headers helpful snippet.<pre><code class=\"language-json\">{\n    &quot;Authorization&quot;: &quot;@{body('Parse Access Token')?['token_type']} @{body('Parse Access Token')?['access_token']}&quot;,\n    &quot;Accept&quot;: &quot;application/json;odata=verbose&quot;,\n    &quot;Content-Type&quot;: &quot;text/xml&quot;\n}\n</code></pre>\n</li>\n<li>Body gets fun. You've got a few values to substitute.<pre><code class=\"language-xml\">&lt;Request AddExpandoFieldTypeSuffix=&quot;true&quot; SchemaVersion=&quot;15.0.0.0&quot; LibraryVersion=&quot;15.0.0.0&quot; ApplicationName=&quot;{YOUR_APP}&quot; xmlns=&quot;http://schemas.microsoft.com/sharepoint/clientquery/2009&quot;&gt;\n    &lt;Actions&gt;\n        &lt;SetProperty Id=&quot;1&quot; ObjectPathId=&quot;2&quot; Name=&quot;Owner&quot;&gt;\n            &lt;Parameter ObjectPathId=&quot;3&quot; /&gt;\n        &lt;/SetProperty&gt;\n        &lt;Method Name=&quot;Update&quot; Id=&quot;4&quot; ObjectPathId=&quot;2&quot; /&gt;\n    &lt;/Actions&gt;\n    &lt;ObjectPaths&gt;\n        &lt;Identity Id=&quot;2&quot; Name=&quot;740c6a0b-85e2-48a0-a494-e0f1759d4aa7:site:{SPSITE_ID}:g:{TARGET_GROUP_ID}&quot; /&gt;\n        &lt;Identity Id=&quot;3&quot; Name=&quot;740c6a0b-85e2-48a0-a494-e0f1759d4aa7:site:{SPSITE_ID}:g:{NEW_OWNER_GROUP_ID}&quot; /&gt;\n    &lt;/ObjectPaths&gt;\n&lt;/Request&gt;\n</code></pre>\n<ul>\n<li>YOUR_APP = Identity your app. This isn't really that important.</li>\n<li>SPSITE_ID = this is the GUID of the site collection you're working with.\nDon't include the curly braces.</li>\n<li>TARGET_GROUP_ID = this is the integer of the group that needs an ownership\nchange</li>\n<li>NEW_OWNER_GROUP_ID = this is the integer of the group that will be the\nowner</li>\n</ul>\n</li>\n</ol>\n<h2>Schemas</h2>\n<p>These are some helpful schemas to paste in to get values back from REST calls.</p>\n<h3>Get Role Definition or Group Id</h3>\n<ul>\n<li>Example URLs:<pre><code>https://{TENANT}/{SPSITE_URL}/_api/web/roledefinitions/getbyname('Contribute')/id\nhttps://{TENANT}/{SPSITE_URL}/_api/web/sitegroups/getbyname('Some%20Group')/id\n</code></pre>\n</li>\n<li>Schema:<pre><code class=\"language-json\">{\n    &quot;type&quot;: &quot;object&quot;,\n    &quot;properties&quot;: {\n        &quot;d&quot;: {\n            &quot;type&quot;: &quot;object&quot;,\n            &quot;properties&quot;: {\n                &quot;Id&quot;: { &quot;type&quot;: &quot;number&quot; }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n</code></pre>\n</li>\n</ul>\n<h3>Get List or Library Id</h3>\n<ul>\n<li>Schema:<pre><code class=\"language-json\">{\n    &quot;type&quot;: &quot;object&quot;,\n    &quot;properties&quot;: {\n        &quot;d&quot;: {\n            &quot;type&quot;: &quot;object&quot;,\n            &quot;properties&quot;: {\n                &quot;Id&quot;: { &quot;type&quot;: &quot;string&quot; }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n</code></pre>\n</li>\n</ul>\n",

        "rawInput": "\nThis post will contain whatever handy information I come across for utilizing\nthe SharePoint REST APIs with Microsoft Flow.\n\n<!--more-->\n\nWhy would you want to do this? Because there aren't enough actions to accomplish\nall the things you'd want to do with SharePoint via Flow.\n\nThe first section of this guide comes from combining a few different blog posts,\nbut I found\n[Calling the SharePoint Online API from within Microsoft Flow by ROBRECHT-VAN-CAENEGEM](https://blogs.u2u.be/u2u/post/calling-the-sharepoint-online-api-from-within-microsoft-flow)\nto be the most useful. It's got pictures!\n\n# How does this work?\n\n-   Microsoft Flow can send generic HTTP requests, with custom headers, body, etc.\n-   For Flow to authenticate to SharePoint during the REST calls, we'll make use\n    of the access tokens typically used for SharePoint Addins/Apps\n\n# Intial Setup\n\nWe're going to need four pieces of data:\n\n-   **CLIENTID**: Unique id assigned to your add-in registration\n-   **CLIENTSECRET**: Secret value used by your add-in registration\n-   **REALM**: This is the unique id assigned to your SharePoint Online tenant.\n-   **TENANT**: The hostname of your tenant (e.g. example.sharepoint.com)\n\n## Obtain the CLIENTID and CLIENTSECRET values\n\n1.  On the SharePoint site that you need to communicate with, navigate to\n    AppRegNew page\n    ```\n    <your site's URL>/_layouts/15/appregnew.aspx\n    ```\n2.  Fill in the information.\n\n    -   Client Id: <<Generate It!>>\n    -   Client Secret: <<Generate It!>>\n    -   Title: <<Project Name Flow>>\n    -   App Domain: localhost\n    -   Redirect URI: https:/localhost\n\n3.  Store the Client Id and Secret. We're going to need it for the next step.\n4.  Click the _Create_ button.\n5.  Navigate to the AppInv page `<your site's URL>/_layouts/15/appinv.aspx`\n6.  Put the _Client Id_ into the _App Id_ text box and look it up.\n7.  Paste the following XML into the _Permission Request XML_ box\n    ([modify as needed for what scope and right you need](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/sharepoint/dev/sp-add-ins/add-in-permissions-in-sharepoint)):\n    ```xml\n    <AppPermissionRequests AllowAppOnlyPolicy=\"true\">\n        <AppPermissionRequest Scope=\"http://sharepoint/content/sitecollection\" Right=\"FullControl\" />\n    </AppPermissionRequests>\n    ```\n8.  Click the _Create_ button.\n\n## Obtain the REALM value\n\n1.  On the SharePoint site that you just finished app registration on, navigate\n    to the AppPrincipals page\n    ```\n    /_layouts/15/AppPrincipals.aspx\n    ```\n2.  You should see your recently registered app principle along with an App\n    Identifier. The last section of the App Identifier, after the @, is the\n    REALM value.\n\n## Setup Authentication in Flow\n\n1.  In your created flow, directly after the trigger, do the following:\n2.  Create a new **Parse JSON** action, renamed to _Authentication Values_,\n    filling in your own values and using the below schema.\n    -   Content:\n        ```json\n        {\n            \"realm\": \"{REALM}\",\n            \"clientId\": \"{CLIENTID}\",\n            \"clientSecret\": \"{CLIENTSECRET}\",\n            \"principal\": \"00000003-0000-0ff1-ce00-000000000000\",\n            \"tenant\": \"{TENANT}\"\n        }\n        ```\n    -   Schema:\n        ```json\n        {\n            \"type\": \"object\",\n            \"properties\": {\n                \"realm\": { \"type\": \"string\" },\n                \"clientId\": { \"type\": \"string\" },\n                \"clientSecret\": { \"type\": \"string\" },\n                \"principal\": { \"type\": \"string\" },\n                \"tenant\": { \"type\": \"string\" }\n            }\n        }\n        ```\n3.  Create a new **Initialize variable** action, renamed to Initialize\n    AccessTokenBody, with the following values: - Name: `AccessTokenBody` -\n    Type: String - Value:\n    `concat('grant_type=client_credentials&client_id=', body('Authentication_Values')?['clientId'], '@', body('Authentication_Values')?['realm'], '&client_secret=', body('Authentication_Values')?['clientSecret'], '&resource=', body('Authentication_Values')?['principal'], '/', body('Authentication_Values')?['tenant'], '@', body('Authentication_Values')?['realm']) `\n4.  Create a new **HTTP - HTTP** action.\n5.  Rename it _Get Access Token_\n6.  Fill in the values:\n\n    -   **Method**: POST\n    -   **Uri**:\n        `https://accounts.accesscontrol.windows.net/@{body('Authentication_Values')?['realm']}/tokens/oauth/2`\n    -   **Headers**:\n        ```json\n        {\n            \"Content-Type\": \"application/x-www-form-urlencoded\"\n        }\n        ```\n    -   **Body**: the _AccessTokenBody_ variable\n\n7.  Add a new **Parse JSON** action and rename it **Parse Access Token**.\n8.  Content should be set to the Body parameter from the previuos step. Schema\n    should be set to the following:\n    ```json\n    {\n        \"type\": \"object\",\n        \"properties\": {\n            \"token_type\": { \"type\": \"string\" },\n            \"access_token\": { \"type\": \"string\" }\n        }\n    }\n    ```\n\nWith this setup, you should be able to test your FLOW and not have it error. You\ncan also check and see the token_type and access_token being parsed. Note that\nthe most tricky part of this is getting the Body variable of step 6 setup\ncorrectly. Note that my value depends upon you having renamed the steps as I\ninstructed to work.\n\n**You're now ready to start using SharePoint REST APIs in Flow!**\n\n# Helpful Snippets\n\nThis section will be a hodge podge of useful snippets I plan to continue adding\nto.\n\n## General\n\n### Headers\n\nIt's easiest to paste in the headers values of **HTTP - HTTP** actions if it's\nin text mode. Here's what's needed (adjust the name of the action where mine\nsays **Parse Access Token** to match the name of your action that parses the\naccess tokens)\n\n```json\n{\n    \"Authorization\": \"@{body('Parse Access Token')?['token_type']} @{body('Parse Access Token')?['access_token']}\",\n    \"Accept\": \"application/json;odata=verbose\",\n    \"Content-Type\": \"application/json;odata=verbose\"\n}\n```\n\n## Groups and Permissions\n\n### Set the Owner of a SharePoint Group to another SharePoint Group\n\nSo, this apparently has been broken via typical REST API method calls for quite\nsome time. There is a working alternative though - manually construct the call\nthat the CSOM library would have made. The best resource I found for this is\n[Jason Lee's blog post: Custom Workflow Activity for Setting a SharePoint Group Owner](http://www.jrjlee.com/2014/01/custom-workflow-activity-for-setting.html),\nwhich is specifically talking about doing this within a SharePoint 2013 model\nworkflow. We'll modify it slightly.\n\n1.  Start with your standard **HTTP - HTTP** action.\n2.  Method = POST\n3.  Uri (adjust values for your environment) =\n    `https://{TENANT}/{SPSITE_URL}/_vti_bin/client.svc/ProcessQuery`\n4.  Headers are slightly different than the Headers helpful snippet.\n    ```json\n    {\n        \"Authorization\": \"@{body('Parse Access Token')?['token_type']} @{body('Parse Access Token')?['access_token']}\",\n        \"Accept\": \"application/json;odata=verbose\",\n        \"Content-Type\": \"text/xml\"\n    }\n    ```\n5.  Body gets fun. You've got a few values to substitute.\n    ```xml\n    <Request AddExpandoFieldTypeSuffix=\"true\" SchemaVersion=\"15.0.0.0\" LibraryVersion=\"15.0.0.0\" ApplicationName=\"{YOUR_APP}\" xmlns=\"http://schemas.microsoft.com/sharepoint/clientquery/2009\">\n        <Actions>\n            <SetProperty Id=\"1\" ObjectPathId=\"2\" Name=\"Owner\">\n                <Parameter ObjectPathId=\"3\" />\n            </SetProperty>\n            <Method Name=\"Update\" Id=\"4\" ObjectPathId=\"2\" />\n        </Actions>\n        <ObjectPaths>\n            <Identity Id=\"2\" Name=\"740c6a0b-85e2-48a0-a494-e0f1759d4aa7:site:{SPSITE_ID}:g:{TARGET_GROUP_ID}\" />\n            <Identity Id=\"3\" Name=\"740c6a0b-85e2-48a0-a494-e0f1759d4aa7:site:{SPSITE_ID}:g:{NEW_OWNER_GROUP_ID}\" />\n        </ObjectPaths>\n    </Request>\n    ```\n    -   YOUR_APP = Identity your app. This isn't really that important.\n    -   SPSITE_ID = this is the GUID of the site collection you're working with.\n        Don't include the curly braces.\n    -   TARGET_GROUP_ID = this is the integer of the group that needs an ownership\n        change\n    -   NEW_OWNER_GROUP_ID = this is the integer of the group that will be the\n        owner\n\n## Schemas\n\nThese are some helpful schemas to paste in to get values back from REST calls.\n\n### Get Role Definition or Group Id\n\n-   Example URLs:\n    ```\n    https://{TENANT}/{SPSITE_URL}/_api/web/roledefinitions/getbyname('Contribute')/id\n    https://{TENANT}/{SPSITE_URL}/_api/web/sitegroups/getbyname('Some%20Group')/id\n    ```\n-   Schema:\n    ```json\n    {\n        \"type\": \"object\",\n        \"properties\": {\n            \"d\": {\n                \"type\": \"object\",\n                \"properties\": {\n                    \"Id\": { \"type\": \"number\" }\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n    ```\n\n### Get List or Library Id\n\n-   Schema:\n    ```json\n    {\n        \"type\": \"object\",\n        \"properties\": {\n            \"d\": {\n                \"type\": \"object\",\n                \"properties\": {\n                    \"Id\": { \"type\": \"string\" }\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n    ```\n",
